newsitem.title: USA: FDA panel hears laxative ingredient carcinogenic.
newsitem.headline: FDA panel hears laxative ingredient carcinogenic.

text.p: A panel of federal health advisers on Wednesday heard new data that an ingredient common to stimulant laxatives may cause cancer in mice when given in high doses, but the committee did not make a decision if the data may be applicable to humans.
The panel met through the afternoon in a closed session and will report to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) within a few weeks on its conclusions.
The ingredient, phenolphthalein, is found in many laxatives, including Ex-Lax, made by Novartis Pharmaceuticals. Ex-Lax had sales of $41 million in 1996.

Novartis vice president Mark Gelder told the panel that Ex-Lax has been safely used "for over 90 years," and that the new data presented by the National Toxicology Program (NTP) should not cause any additional concern.
Novartis had not previously seen the data, and asked the FDA to work with the firm to review it before reaching any conclusions about phenolphthalein's status.

The FDA panel has met twice before to consider animal data on phenolphthalein. In April 1996, the committee concluded it needed more information before it could determine whether animal studies were relevant to humans. In May 1996, the FDA told manufacturers it was reclassifying phenolphthalein from "safe and effective" to "more data needed."

The NTP conducted further studies, using genetically-engineered mice that received two different types of the p53 gene, found in many tumors. In the mice given extremely high doses -- twenty times the level of human consumption -- of phenolphthalein over six months, there was a statistically significantly high rate of tumor formation and of early deaths due to cancer.
Several other ingredients used in stimulant laxatives, including senna and bisacodyl, are also suspected of being carcinogenic and were also reclassified by the FDA last May.
Lorna Totman, director of scientific affairs at the Non-Prescription Drug Manufacturers Association, said that manufacturers have already submitted data to the agency proving safety.
Schering-Plough Corp issued a press release the day before the meeting stating that its laxatives Correctol and Feen-A-Mint, do not contain phenolphthalein.
